acs_2022_median_household_income.description: Median household income in the past 12 months (in 2022 inflation-adjusted dollars) for each U.S. state and Puerto Rico.

variables.NAME: State or territory name
variables.state: State FIPS code as a two-digit string; 72 is Puerto Rico

acs_2022_median_household_income.geographic_coverage: 50 states, District of Columbia, Puerto Rico (state:* in ACS API)
notes: Values are as returned directly by the ACS API; they are provided as strings in the raw data array.
To independently verify, visit the API example URL and compare the returned JSON array to the data stored in state_data_raw.json under acs_2022_median_household_income.data.

acs_2022_race_B02001_subset.description: Total population and selected race-alone counts (White alone, Black or African American alone, Asian alone) for each state and Puerto Rico.

variables.state: State FIPS code as a two-digit string; 72 is Puerto Rico

acs_2022_race_B02001_subset.geographic_coverage: 50 states, District of Columbia, Puerto Rico (state:* in ACS API)
notes: Only a subset of B02001 race categories is included here (White alone, Black or African American alone, Asian alone). Additional race categories can be added later by querying the same table.
Values are counts (not percentages). Percent shares by race can be computed in your application by dividing each race count by B02001_001E for that state.
To verify, call the API example URL and compare the returned rows to the data stored in state_data_raw.json under acs_2022_race_B02001_subset.data.

acs_2022_subject_socioeconomic.description: State-level socio-economic percentages from ACS 2022: poverty rate, share of adults with a bachelor's degree or higher, and unemployment rate.
tables: S1701 (Poverty Status in the Past 12 Months)

variables.S1701_C03_001E: Estimate!!Percent below poverty level!!Population for whom poverty status is determined
variables.S1501_C02_015E: Estimate!!Percent!!AGE BY EDUCATIONAL ATTAINMENT!!Population 25 years and over!!Bachelor's degree or higher
variables.state: State FIPS code as a two-digit string; 72 is Puerto Rico

acs_2022_subject_socioeconomic.geographic_coverage: 50 states, District of Columbia, Puerto Rico (state:* in ACS subject API)
acs_2022_subject_socioeconomic.time_coverage: 2018-2022 survey period, reported as 2022 1-year subject estimates
notes: All three variables are percentages, expressed as values like 16.2 (percent) rather than 0.162.
To verify, call the API example URL and compare the returned rows to the data stored in state_data_raw.json under acs_2022_subject_socioeconomic.data.

vsrr_2023Q1_firearm_related_injury_age_a.description: Provisional, age-adjusted death rates (per 100,000) for firearm-related injury by state, for the 12 months ending with 2023 Q1.
vsrr_2023Q1_firearm_related_injury_age_a.source_organization: National Center for Health Statistics (NCHS), Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
vsrr_2023Q1_firearm_related_injury_age_a.dataset: NCHS - VSRR Quarterly provisional estimates for selected indicators
vsrr_2023Q1_firearm_related_injury_age_a.measure: Age-adjusted death rate per 100,000 population for firearm-related injuries.
vsrr_2023Q1_firearm_related_injury_age_a.geographic_coverage: 50 states and District of Columbia (fields rate_alabama, rate_alaska, ..., rate_wyoming)
important_caveats: These are provisional estimates and may differ slightly from final NVSS mortality data.
State fields are provided as lowercased names prefixed with 'rate_', for example 'rate_alabama', 'rate_california', etc.
Rates are age-adjusted using a standard CDC methodology; they should not be interpreted as crude (unadjusted) rates.
verification_instructions: Open the api_example_url in a browser or via an HTTP client.
Confirm that the single JSON object returned matches the object stored in state_data_raw.json under vsrr_2023Q1_firearm_related_injury_age_adjusted_death_rates.data.

vsrr_2023Q1_homicide_age_adjusted_death_.description: Provisional, age-adjusted death rates (per 100,000) for homicide by state, for the 12 months ending with 2023 Q1.
vsrr_2023Q1_homicide_age_adjusted_death_.source_organization: National Center for Health Statistics (NCHS), CDC
vsrr_2023Q1_homicide_age_adjusted_death_.dataset: NCHS - VSRR Quarterly provisional estimates for selected indicators
vsrr_2023Q1_homicide_age_adjusted_death_.measure: Age-adjusted death rate per 100,000 population for homicide deaths (all mechanisms).
vsrr_2023Q1_homicide_age_adjusted_death_.geographic_coverage: 50 states and District of Columbia (fields rate_alabama, rate_alaska, ..., rate_wyoming)
important_caveats: Provisional mortality data are subject to revision and may not exactly match later final NVSS/WONDER tabulations.
Homicide here is defined per ICD-10 underlying cause codes used by NCHS for this indicator (see dataset documentation on data.cdc.gov for exact code list).
verification_instructions: Confirm that the returned JSON object matches the object stored in state_data_raw.json under vsrr_2023Q1_homicide_age_adjusted_death_rates.data.

vsrr_2023Q1_drug_overdose_age_adjusted_d.description: Provisional, age-adjusted death rates (per 100,000) for drug overdose deaths by state, for the 12 months ending with 2023 Q1.
vsrr_2023Q1_drug_overdose_age_adjusted_d.source_organization: National Center for Health Statistics (NCHS), CDC
vsrr_2023Q1_drug_overdose_age_adjusted_d.dataset: NCHS - VSRR Quarterly provisional estimates for selected indicators
vsrr_2023Q1_drug_overdose_age_adjusted_d.measure: Age-adjusted death rate per 100,000 population for drug overdose deaths.
vsrr_2023Q1_drug_overdose_age_adjusted_d.geographic_coverage: 50 states and District of Columbia (fields rate_alabama, rate_alaska, ..., rate_wyoming)
important_caveats: Provisional overdose mortality estimates are based on a flow of death certificate data and can change as investigations are completed.
The dataset uses an NCHS definition of drug overdose deaths based on ICD-10 underlying cause-of-death codes (see dataset documentation).
verification_instructions: Confirm that the returned JSON object matches the object stored in state_data_raw.json under vsrr_2023Q1_drug_overdose_age_adjusted_death_rates.data.

brfss_depression_reference.description: Reference to BRFSS prevalence data for lifetime diagnosis of depression among adults by state.
brfss_depression_reference.source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
brfss_depression_reference.dataset: Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System (BRFSS) Prevalence Data (2011 to present)
brfss_depression_reference.question: Ever told you that you have a form of depression? (questionid=ADDEPEV3)
brfss_depression_reference.measure: Crude prevalence (percent) of adults who report ever having been told they have a form of depression.
notes: Each row includes fields such as locationabbr (state postal code), locationdesc (state name), data_value (prevalence percent), and confidence limits.
As with heavy drinking, values can be fetched on demand via the documented query and integrated into the derived state metrics.
Use both heavy drinking and depression cautiously: they are self-reported BRFSS survey estimates, subject to sampling error and nonresponse bias.

brfss_heavy_drinking_reference.description: Reference to BRFSS prevalence data for heavy drinking by state; values are not fully inlined in state_data_raw.json yet, but the exact API slice is documented here for later integration.
brfss_heavy_drinking_reference.source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
brfss_heavy_drinking_reference.dataset: Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System (BRFSS) Prevalence Data (2011 to present)
brfss_heavy_drinking_reference.suggested_api_query_for_state_level_over: year=2022&topic=Heavy Drinking&break_out=Overall&break_out_category=Overall&data_value_type=Crude Prevalence&response=Meet criteria for heavy drinking
notes: When you are ready to add alcohol metrics, you can fetch state-level heavy drinking prevalence by calling the BRFSS API with the suggested query.
Each row includes fields such as locationabbr (state postal code), locationdesc (state name), data_value (prevalence percent), and confidence limits.

Because the BRFSS slice is relatively large and you may wish to apply your own filters (e.g., age-adjusted vs crude), the raw numeric values were not fully duplicated into state_data_raw.json in this iteration.

giffords_gun_law_scorecard_2022.description: State gun law strength grades and rankings from GIFFORDS Law Center Annual Gun Law Scorecard, released February 2022.
giffords_gun_law_scorecard_2022.source_organization: GIFFORDS Law Center to Prevent Gun Violence

variables.grade: Letter grade (A, A-, B+, B, B-, C+, C, C-, D+, D, D-, F) indicating strength of state gun laws
variables.rank: Numerical ranking from 1 (strongest gun laws) to 50 (weakest gun laws)

giffords_gun_law_scorecard_2022.time_coverage: 2022 scorecard (released February 2022, evaluating gun laws as of end of 2021)
methodology: GIFFORDS legal experts track and analyze gun legislation in all 50 states throughout the year.
Laws and policies are assigned point values based on their respective strengths or weaknesses.
States are ranked and given letter grades based on total points.
Grades are compared to CDC gun death rates to demonstrate correlation between strong laws and lower death rates.
important_caveats: Grades reflect GIFFORDS Law Center's assessment of gun law strength, which is one perspective on gun policy.
The scorecard evaluates laws on the books, not enforcement or compliance.
Rankings may shift year-to-year as states pass new legislation.
verification_instructions: Visit https://giffords.org/lawcenter/resources/scorecard2022/ to view the interactive scorecard.
Select individual states on the map or use the table view to verify grades and rankings.
Press release at press_release_url confirms specific grades mentioned (CA=A, NJ=A, NY=A-, MD=A-, CO=B+, IA=F, MO=F, MT=F).
